laws.rule: Oita Prefecture's accommodation tax starts on 1 June 2027. It is charged per person per night at hotels, ryokan (Japanese inns), simple lodgings and registered home-stays (minpaku), by the room charge excluding meals and consumption tax: JPY 100 under JPY 5,000 (about A$0.90); JPY 200 from JPY 5,000 to 19,999 (about A$1.80); JPY 500 from JPY 20,000 to 99,999 (about A$4.51); JPY 2,000 from JPY 100,000 (about A$18.05), RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82. School trips are exempt with a certificate from the school; sports tournaments and club training camps are not.
laws.heading: 大分県宿泊税

laws.rule: In the central 'enhanced litter-prevention zone' of Oita City, smoking on the street is banned except at designated smoking spots. Littering is banned too, and dog owners must pick up droppings. The administrative fine is JPY 2,000 (about A$18.05, RBA rate of 30 October 2026). The ordinance began on 1 July 2006; heated tobacco has been covered since 1 July 2019. The zone boundary is on a map on the city page.

festivals.what: Tennenji Shujo Onie (Tennen-ji temple, Nagaiwaya, Bungotakada City, Kunisaki Peninsula): a night fire festival praying for good harvests and good health, held on the 7th day of the first month of the old lunar calendar, usually in February (23 February in 2026). Red and black oni, seen here as forms of the Buddha, swing large torches. It is a nationally designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property. The city lists no photography fee; vehicles cannot enter the site, and parking is nearby. The date moves each year with the lunar calendar.

moving_calendars.what: Shujo Onie dates follow the old lunar calendar (7th day of the first month at Tennen-ji), so the Gregorian date changes each year; confirm with Bungotakada City before going.
